score_comment_short: Your onboarding example needs a result a recruiter can understand.
score_comment_long: Owners, checkpoints, and an on-time roadmap make the experience easy to follow. The weaker part is the evidence of results: 'improving productivity' is a claim without a measure.
first_impression: A recruiter can see experience organizing launches and coordinating a roadmap. It is harder to tell which decisions you made yourself, rather than helped carry out.
score_plain: Readability is your highest-rated area; impact is the lowest. Spend your revision time on the results of your work before changing the layout.
biggest_gap_example: "Led onboarding work across the company, improving productivity." What got easier or faster for the people you onboarded?
first_impression_takeaway: What did your onboarding work improve?
summary: Your experience centers on getting work done across teams. The launch owners, checkpoints, and quarterly roadmap are relevant examples for program management. For product management, the resume would also need examples of how you chose priorities using data or customer feedback, if you have that experience.
strengths: The launch example includes owners and checkpoints. Those details show how you organized the project.
You say the quarterly roadmap was delivered on time. Keep that result; it tells us more than a list of responsibilities would.
Your onboarding, launch, and stakeholder work is relevant to Program Manager roles.
gaps: 'Improving productivity' doesn't explain what got easier or faster after onboarding.
The skills list uses broad terms without identifying the planning or launch methods you used.
The resume doesn't make clear whether you want to coordinate delivery or set product priorities. That affects which examples you should put first.
